title: Hosting: A2A, AG-UI, OpenAI-compatible and Foundry hosted
summary: An agent or workflow becomes a service by choosing who owns the host: your own ASP.NET or Python server with protocol adapters (OpenAI-compatible, A2A, AG-UI), Foundry hosted agents, or the Durable Extension.
useIf: Clients other than your own code must call the agent, and you must decide who owns routing, auth, sessions and scaling.
avoidIf: You only run agents in-process inside an existing service and expose nothing new.

explain.md: **Self-hosting.** In .NET, `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting` (prerelease) registers agents and workflows in the generic host: `AddAIAgent`, `AddWorkflow` and `AddAsAIAgent`. Protocol packages add endpoints: **OpenAI-compatible** Chat Completions and Responses (`MapOpenAIChatCompletions`, `MapOpenAIResponses`, `MapOpenAIConversations`), **A2A** (`Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.A2A.AspNetCore`, with an Agent Card; Python uses `A2AExecutor` from `agent-framework-a2a` inside the a2a-sdk server) and **AG-UI** (`MapAGUIServer`, Server-Sent Events for web agent UIs with tool rendering, approvals and state sync). Your app owns auth, routing, request validation and storage. No general-purpose durable `AgentSessionStore` ships, so supply one; scope persisted sessions by an authenticated user or tenant, because a continuation id identifies a session but does not prove ownership [[tr31]] [[tr32]] [[tr33]] [[tr34]].

**Foundry hosted agents** (service GA; Python `agent-framework-foundry-hosting` Beta, .NET `.Foundry.Hosting` preview; checked 2026-10-13). A container with a platform identity per agent, persisted `$HOME` and files, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Two protocols: **Responses** (`ResponsesHostServer(agent)`, recommended start; the platform manages history, streaming and sessions) and **Invocations** (`InvocationsHostServer`, full control of payload and streaming such as AG-UI). Python `history_source` picks who supplies model history: `agent_server` (default), `service` or `agent`. Default hosted stores are namespaced by platform user and sandbox session, use ETag writes and expire sessions 30 days after last write. Host a workflow natively with `workflow=` and a `parse_response` callback; hosting `agent=workflow.as_agent()` is deprecated because a `WorkflowAgent` keeps state in memory [[tr35]].

blocks.code:
from agent_framework_foundry_hosting import ResponsesHostServer, CheckpointStoreProvider

# Foundry hosted: agent instance, or a factory called once per request
server = ResponsesHostServer(agent)          # history_source='agent_server' by default
server.run()

# native workflow on the Responses protocol
server = ResponsesHostServer(
    workflow=build_workflow,                 # request-aware factory, fresh graph each call
    parse_response=parse_response,
    checkpoint_store_provider=CheckpointStoreProvider(
        allowed_checkpoint_types=['my_app.models:Ticket']),
)

# self-host A2A with the a2a-sdk server
handler = DefaultRequestHandler(agent_executor=A2AExecutor(agent, stream=True),
    task_store=InMemoryTaskStore(), agent_card=public_agent_card)

whereToUse: Self-host when the agent must live inside an existing ASP.NET service with your auth and network rules
OpenAI-compatible endpoints so any OpenAI SDK client can call your agent
A2A so other teams' or vendors' agents can discover and call yours through an Agent Card
AG-UI for web or mobile chat with streaming, approvals and shared state
Foundry hosted agents when you want managed identity, endpoints and session persistence for a container

use: Self-host for maximum control and existing infrastructure
Foundry hosted for managed scaling, an Entra identity per agent and Responses endpoints
Responses first: add Invocations later for custom payloads, webhooks or custom streaming
avoid: Using DevUI in production: the docs call it a sample not intended for production use
Letting clients choose session ids without scoping to a user or tenant
Reusing one stateful agent or WorkflowAgent instance for different users
flips: You need durable waits and scale to zero: add the Durable Extension on Functions
Clients are agents from other organisations: expose A2A with an Agent Card and real auth, not only an OpenAI endpoint

pitfalls.cause: Client-supplied continuation ids were trusted without an isolation key
pitfalls.fix: Use an isolation key (for example `IsolationKeyScopedAgentSessionStore`) tied to the authenticated user or tenant

pitfalls.symptom: Sessions vanish after a restart on a self-hosted .NET service
pitfalls.cause: `InMemoryAgentSessionStore` loses state when the process exits
pitfalls.fix: Implement a durable `AgentSessionStore` keyed by agent id and opaque session id

pitfalls.cause: A `WorkflowAgent` instance holds state in memory and was reused across requests
pitfalls.fix: Host natively with `workflow=` and a per-request factory that builds a fresh graph

scenarios.title: Expose an agent to partner agents
scenarios.situation: A logistics company wants partner companies' agents to request shipment quotes from its agent. Partners use different frameworks. Auth must be per partner and calls are asynchronous at times.
unknowns: Is an Agent Card published publicly?
scenarios.question: Which protocol do you expose?

options.name: A2A with an Agent Card, per-partner auth and task support, hosted on your service or Foundry
options.why: A2A is the interop protocol for opaque agents across vendors and handles long-running tasks.
options.tradeoff: Python A2A is Beta and .NET preview, and v1 migration changed registration APIs in 2026.

options.name: OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint only
options.why: Any OpenAI SDK client can call it.
options.tradeoff: Not agent-to-agent discovery, and partners must build around a chat-style API.

options.name: AG-UI endpoint
options.why: AG-UI targets web or mobile agent UIs, not agent-to-agent calls.
options.tradeoff: Right for your own front end.

flips.if: Partners only use OpenAI SDKs and tasks are short
You want managed identity and scaling
flips.then: Host the A2A protocol on Foundry hosted agents.

scenarios.takeaway: Pick the protocol by who the caller is: a person's UI, an SDK client or another agent.

scenarios.title: Internal assistant with a small platform team
scenarios.situation: A two-person team must ship an internal assistant on Azure in six weeks. No one wants to operate containers or write session storage. Data stays in the Azure tenant.
unknowns: Is a preview hosting package acceptable?
scenarios.question: How do you host?

options.name: Foundry hosted agent with the Responses protocol and the default platform session stores
options.why: Managed identity, endpoints and scoped session persistence remove most ops work, and the service is GA.
options.tradeoff: Framework hosting packages are Beta or preview, and you accept the platform's limits.

options.name: Self-host in ASP.NET with your own session store
options.tradeoff: You build auth, session isolation, scaling and observability glue.

options.name: Run DevUI for everyone
options.why: DevUI is a sample not intended for production.
options.tradeoff: Fine for demos on a developer machine.

scenarios.takeaway: A small team should rent the platform; control costs engineering time.

quiz.q: Match each protocol to its purpose.

pairs.r: Agent discovery, messaging and tasks between agents
Streaming events for web agent UIs with approvals and state
Full control of the HTTP payload and streaming

quiz.explain: Start with Responses and add Invocations for custom payloads. A2A is for agent-to-agent; AG-UI for user interfaces.

quiz.q: A self-hosted agent accepts a `conversation id` from clients and loads the matching session. What is missing?
options: Scoping the session lookup by the authenticated user or tenant
quiz.explain: A continuation id identifies a session but does not prove ownership. Scope persisted sessions with an isolation key before accepting client ids.

flashcards.front: Which Foundry hosting protocol is recommended first?
flashcards.back: Responses (OpenAI-compatible `/responses`, platform-managed history). Add Invocations later for custom payloads or streaming.

flashcards.front: Does MAF ship a durable session store for self-hosting?
flashcards.back: No general-purpose durable `AgentSessionStore` ships. Implement your own, keyed by agent id and an opaque session id.

flashcards.front: What do the docs say about DevUI?
flashcards.back: It is a sample app not intended for production: web UI, tracing and an OpenAI-compatible API for local development.
